In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have found evidence for a major asymmetric ice trap at 60 au in a warm Herbig disk with low gas to solid ratios, which is the first time this is observed.

dust traps provide an efficient mechanism for the delivery of ice to the warm molecular layers of the disk, where efficient ice chemistry can take place, resulting in high gas phase molecular abundances.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the chemistry in disks is more complex than previously assumed, with the presence of icy pebbles being a key ingredient for complex organic chemistry.
we have found the first evidence for the formation of complex organic molecules at dust traps.
the chemistry in the disk around IRS 48 is dominated by the presence of a pebble trap.
The main takeaway from our work is that
dust traps can provide a mechanism for efficient delivery of complex organic material from the disk midplane to the warm molecular layers, and thus to planet formation regions.
dust traps can be important for setting the chemistry in the outer disk regions, where giant planets form, and where complex organic chemistry is thought to take place.
pebble concentration in dust traps is an important mechanism for the formation of warm, complex organic molecules in the midplane of planet forming disks.
